title: Wavelength and frequency
blurb: Higher frequency, shorter wave. 300 divided by megahertz gives meters.

lines.caption: A radio wave travels at the speed of light: about 300 million meters every second.
Frequency is how many cycles the wave makes each second. It is measured in hertz.
Wavelength is the length of one cycle.
All radio waves travel at the same speed. So as frequency goes up, wavelength gets shorter.
Here is the shortcut. Wavelength in meters equals 300 divided by the frequency in megahertz.
At 146 MHz, 300 divided by 146 is about 2 meters.
At 50 MHz, 300 divided by 50 is 6 meters. Lower frequency, longer wave.
That is why ham bands are also named by wavelength: the 2 meter band, the 6 meter band.
